rule.title: Game Rules
rule.content:
【Objective】

Move your pieces on a 7×7 board and build walls to carve out your own ‘territory’ (an enclosed area containing only your pieces). When the game ends, count the squares in each player’s territory; the player with the most wins.

【Equipment & Players】
 • Board: 7×7 squares
 • Players:
   • 2-player: Red and Blue, each with 4 pieces
   • 3/4-player: Add Yellow/Light Blue, each color has 2 pieces
 • Walls: Unlimited, color-coded by player

【Game Flow】
Placement Phase
 • 2-player: Starting positions fixed: Red [1,1],[5,5]; Blue [1,5],[5,1]. The other two are placed alternately: Red, Blue, Blue, Red
 • 3/4-player: Each player places 2 pieces, in alternating order (e.g. A→B→C→C→B→A)

Action Phase (turn-based)
 • Red takes the first turn
 1. Choose any of your pieces that can still act
 2. Move 0, 1, or 2 steps:
   • Each step must be up, down, left, or right
   • Cannot cross or pass through walls or other pieces
 3. After moving, you must place a wall on an open side of that piece’s square (even if you moved 0 steps)

【Walls & Borders】
 • The board’s outer edge counts as a wall
 • 2-player: Walls cannot be removed once placed
 • 3/4-player: Each player gets one “wall break” per game, usable on their turn

【Time Limit】
 • 90 seconds per turn
 • If time runs out, a wall is placed randomly and the turn ends

【End Condition】
 • The game ends when all players’ pieces are in separate territories

【Scoring】
 • Each square in a territory is worth 1 point
 • If total scores are tied, the player with the largest single territory wins

【Victory】
 • Highest score wins
 • If both total and largest territory are tied, it’s a draw

── Enjoy the game!

about.title: What is Wall Go?
about.p1: Wall Go is the wall-building territory game from season 2 of Netflix's The Devil's Plan. Two players share a 7×7 board: on every turn you move one of your pieces up to two squares, then drop a wall on one side of it. Walls never come down, so the board slowly splits into sealed rooms. When every piece is locked into its own room, the player with more squares wins.
about.p2: This is a free, open-source browser version. There is nothing to install and no account to create: pick two-player or AI, and play.

howTo.title: How to play Wall Go
steps: Placement: each player starts with four pieces. Two are fixed for each colour; the other two are placed alternately (Red, Blue, Blue, Red).
Move: Red starts. Choose one of your pieces and move it 0, 1 or 2 squares up, down, left or right. You cannot pass through walls or other pieces.
Build: after moving you must place a wall on an open side of that piece's square, even if you stood still. The board edge already counts as a wall.
Clock: each turn has 90 seconds. If it runs out, a wall is placed at random and the turn ends.
End: the game ends when every piece is sealed into a territory that holds only one colour.
Score: every square in your territory is worth one point. If totals tie, the larger single territory wins; if that ties too, it's a draw.

features.title: Features
items: Two players on one screen, with named players and a running series score
Play against the AI at four levels, from practice to hard
Undo, redo and a move-history slider to rewind any game
Six languages, dark mode, and a layout that works on phones

items.q: Is Wall Go free to play?
items.a: Yes. This version is free, has no ads and needs no account. The code is open source on GitHub.

items.q: Can I play Wall Go against the computer?
items.a: Yes. Choose "vs AI" on the menu and pick one of four levels. You can also choose whether you move first or second.

items.q: Can two people play on one device?
items.a: Yes. Choose "2 Players", enter both names, and pass the device between turns. Wins and draws are tallied across a series.
Not yet. Both players currently need to share a screen. Online play is on the roadmap.

items.q: Where does Wall Go come from?
items.a: Wall Go was played in season 2 of The Devil's Plan, a Korean reality competition on Netflix. The show's version uses the same 7×7 board, movement and wall rules.

items.q: How is this different from the original schaoss/wall-go?
items.a: It is a fork that adds named players, a series scoreboard, a move-history slider and other quality-of-life features. The rules and core gameplay are unchanged.
